correctness.rationale: The two endpoint-product equations are exactly equivalent to c_m(s)=v-((v-u)d/v)(p_m/q_m) and F_m(s)=0. Since p_m,q_m converge uniformly in C^1 to exponentials, every simple strict zero persists for each sufficiently large m with all source theorem hypotheses retained. Theorem 5.3 then produces 3(m+1) distinct genuine NS triangles, and uniform denominator separation yields the right Riemann sum limit of their total scales. The exact 10^40 outward integer-interval verifier certificates a unique simple continuum root for rational d=0.415868, tau=0.67376, all strict inequalities, denominator negativity, monotone integral upper bound and S_infty<0.940465236<10000/10633; thus finite covering factors eventually exceed 10633/10000. No sampled finite m is used as proof of the infinite quantifier.

originality.rationale: The September 2026 primary source explicitly leaves convergence from finite chains open and explains that fixed continuum parameters cannot solve the finite products. The new perturbative scalar-root construction solves both products exactly for all large finite lengths and proves a lower bound that exceeds its rigorous 303-triangle record. Older primary sources treat general covering upper bounds, not this cyclic contact recurrence. value.rationale: The published work isolates the realizability of a continuous contact-chain candidate by finite positive triangles as a named open geometric obstacle. The new theorem solves the regular interior version of that obstacle, constructing exact finite endpoint matches of arbitrarily fine equal-step chains, rather than merely making a minor numerical optimization. Its certified consequence is a strictly improved unconditional planar covering-factor lower bound above 1.0633, beyond the source’s best rigorous finite example; the distinction between true finite constructions and a formal continuum makes the result structurally relevant even without an explicit m_0.
